summary.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 10.5% QoQ to INR161 crore, but gross margin fell 240 bps to 39.5% and EBITDA margin to 14.3% on polymer cost spikes.
summary.overview: Revenue reached INR161 crore (up 10.5% QoQ, up 2% YoY) and polymers processed rose 25% QoQ to 6,323 MT, with utilisation at 64.9%. Raw material costs rose 40-50% from the West Asia crisis, compressing gross margin to 39.5% from 41.9%, with price pass-through partial and time-lagged. Management says the pass-through is largely complete in domestic and is contracted for most exports, with the largest customer's benefit landing in Q2 FY27. Supply-chain disruption (inbound material, containers, logistics) was the main drag, with about INR5.5 crore of sales slipping into July.

segments.name: Domestic India
segments.commentary: About 16% of revenue, roughly INR26 crore, flat YoY and QoQ; management targets 30-35% growth, with 100% price pass-through and orders now flowing.

guidance_outlook: FY27 utilisation target of about 75% on 41,000 MT capacity for the remaining nine months, described as a working assumption dependent on the geopolitical environment.
FY27 revenue/volume growth of at least 15-20% per CFO, backed by order book; EBITDA expected to improve if growth is delivered, but no margin guidance given.
Gross margin and EBITDA recovery expected once raw material environment normalises; management says Q2 FY27 will show full benefit of largest-customer price revision.

Bamboo: Phase 1 at Guwahati (3,000 CBM) machinery arriving mid-August, installation by end-September, commercial contribution from Q4 FY27; Q4 revenue estimated at about 20% of annual run-rate at 75% utilisation. Capex about INR15 crore for Phase 1, may rise for next phase.
Management says EBITDA margin of 18-19% (FY24-FY25) is sustainable at around 80% utilisation; FY27 margin to be better than FY26 but no specific range committed.
capex_capacity: Current installed capacity about 41,000 MT (management also cited 39,000 MT base in opening remarks); utilisation 64.9% in Q1 FY27.
14 new injection moulding machines ordered for about 1,500 MT incremental capacity, arriving Q3 and fully available in Q4 FY27.

A further about 4,000 MT is planned, to be ordered in Q3 with receipt by end of Q4 FY27 if demand confirms; management deferred commitment to pick the right equipment for large-customer projects. Earlier plan was about 6,000 MT in a year.
Bamboo board unit at Madanpur, Guwahati (75,000 sq ft, owned by All-Time Bamboo Pvt Ltd): 3,000 CBM per annum in Phase 1; downstream finishing at Khatalwada, Gujarat.
Khatalwada expansion has raised fixed costs; management says these will be absorbed as utilisation improves.
demand_pricing: Raw material (polymer) costs rose 40-50% over base at peak; management said raw material is about 50-53% of product mix. Selling prices rose about 15% against roughly 20% input impact at a 40% mix.
Domestic: 100% of price increase passed through; largest customer on an eight-week lag, with benefit in Q2 FY27; remaining customers about 50% passed through, with the balance over a longer period.
Management says demand and forecasts have held; supply availability, logistics and raw material inbound were the constraints in April-May, with June improving.
Competition: management views smaller unorganised players under working-capital stress as an opening; large retailers are increasingly focusing on brand and packaging quality.
Bamboo: management says no cannibalisation of plastic business as price points and end consumers differ; bamboo margins are a few points above plastic.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR5 crore of shipment slippage a lost sale or does it carry into subsequent months?
qa_highlights.answer: Not a loss; management quantified about INR5.5 crore (INR3 crore in transit plus INR2.5 crore at factory containers) to be recognised in July 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 75% utilisation target on 39,000 or 41,000 MT?
qa_highlights.answer: On 41,000 MT for the remaining nine months of FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q1 employee expense a fair run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, Q1 is a fair base; any increase will be very small.

qa_highlights.question: Why is volume growth only about 5% QoQ on sales volume, and when does price pass-through show up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said demand is not the issue; raw material availability and logistics were. Q2 should show better demand and the pending price pass-through; one quarter of exceptional pricing growth after normalisation is expected.

qa_highlights.question: Is the remaining 4,000 MT capacity delayed and what is the domestic growth driver?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not a visibility issue; equipment choice depends on customer product lines. Domestic was flat because a full price reset was sought and production was halted, with the largest customer's expansion (20-25 stores in two years, about INR40-50 lakh revenue per store per month) cited as a driver.

qa_highlights.question: Is 15-20% growth achievable, and how will margins move?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said EBITDA will improve if growth comes, but declined to commit to a margin figure; the historical gross margin range is 39-40%.

qa_highlights.question: When will EBITDA margin return to 18-19%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said at around 80% capacity utilisation, which it considers sustainable.

risks_watch: Supply-chain risk: management says inbound polymer availability, container shortages and logistics remain the biggest challenge, and volatility will persist while the conflict continues. About INR5.5 crore of sales is due to be recognised in July 2026.

Margin recovery is timing-dependent: the largest customer's price revision benefits Q2 FY27, the balance of export customers (about 10-15% of business) is only 50% passed through, and management would not commit to a gross or EBITDA margin figure for FY27.

Execution on capacity: 14 machines (about 1,500 MT) arrive Q3 and are fully available in Q4 FY27; the further 4,000 MT is not yet ordered and depends on Q3 demand confirmation. Khatalwada fixed costs will weigh until utilisation rises.
Domestic growth delivery: domestic was flat at about INR26 crore YoY and QoQ in Q1, against a 30-35% target. Watch whether orders convert in Q2 after the 100% price reset.

Bamboo ramp: Phase 1 machinery is in transit and installation is targeted by end-September; commercial contribution is expected only from Q4 FY27, with capex of about INR15 crore that may rise for later phases. Also watch the US large-opportunity discussion, which management has not detailed.
key_quotes: Once the situation genuinely resolved, we expect margin recovery to become visible with a quarter of the environment normalizing.
So, demand is not an issue, the logistic is an issue and raw material availability was an issue.
Please read this as a current working assumptions, given how much still depends on the external geopolitical environment.
Manish Gattani: Nirali, we can't comment on the margin but EBITDA definitely will improve because margin we are doing this 39% historically also.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, order book and the Q2 price pass-through, but cautious and evasive on margins: management repeatedly declined to give a gross or EBITDA margin number and kept the 75% utilisation target explicitly as a working assumption tied to the geopolitical situation.
